# Standard library

<!-- Generated by `nalu doc --all` from the compiler's own tables; do not edit by hand. -->

Every module is always available: there are no imports. Each entry says whether it **can fail** (handle it with `catch`, or let the failure propagate) and whether it **writes** (with `--dry-run` it is only shown, not run). `nalu doc <name>` prints any entry in the terminal.

**Types:** [`str`](#type-str) · [`path`](#type-path) · [`list`](#type-list) · [`map`](#type-map) · [`int`](#type-int) · [`bool`](#type-bool) · [`duration`](#type-duration) · [`secret`](#type-secret) · [`enum`](#type-enum) · [`error`](#type-error)  
**Also:** [built-ins](#built-ins) · [keywords and constants](#keywords-and-constants)

## Module archive

Creates and extracts .tar.gz and .zip archives.

- `archive.tar_create(file: path, dir: path)` (can fail, writes): Creates a .tar.gz with the folder inside (the folder's name is the archive's root).
- `archive.tar_extract(file: path, to: path)` (can fail, writes): Extracts a .tar.gz into `to`, creating it.
- `archive.zip_extract(file: path, to: path)` (can fail, writes): Extracts a .zip into `to`, creating it. Unix: unzip (or BSD tar); Windows: Expand-Archive.

## Module dirs

Home, temporary, config, cache and data folders on each system.

- `dirs.home() -> path`: The user's home folder.
- `dirs.temp() -> path`: The system's temporary folder.
- `dirs.config(app: str) -> path`: The app's config folder: $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/app or ~/.config/app; ~/Library/Application Support/app; %APPDATA%\app.
- `dirs.cache(app: str) -> path`: The app's cache folder on this system.
- `dirs.data(app: str) -> path`: The app's data folder on this system.
- `dirs.cwd() -> path`: The current folder.

## Module encoding

Base64 encoding and decoding of text.

- `encoding.base64_encode(text: str) -> str`: The Base64 of the text's UTF-8 bytes: standard alphabet, `=` padding, one line.
- `encoding.base64_decode(text: str) -> str` (can fail): Decodes Base64 into text. Spaces and line breaks are ignored, the URL-safe alphabet (`-` `_`) and missing `=` padding are accepted; fails if the text isn't Base64 or the bytes aren't UTF-8 text.

## Module env

Environment variables.

- `env.get(name: str) -> str` (can fail): The value of the environment variable; fails if it is not set.
- `env.has(name: str) -> bool`: Whether the environment variable is set.
- `env.set(name: str, value: str)`: Sets the variable for this script and for the commands it runs.
- `env.unset(name: str)`: Removes the variable for this script and for the commands it runs; nothing happens if it is not set.

## Module fs

Files and folders. Writes are only shown with --dry-run.

- `fs.exists(p: path) -> bool`: Whether the path exists (file or folder).
- `fs.is_dir(p: path) -> bool`: Whether the path is an existing folder.
- `fs.is_file(p: path) -> bool`: Whether the path is an existing file.
- `fs.read(p: path) -> str` (can fail): Reads the whole file as UTF-8 text (a BOM is removed).
- `fs.write(p: path, text: str)` (can fail, writes): Creates or overwrites the file: UTF-8 without BOM, `\n` line endings.
- `fs.append(p: path, text: str)` (can fail, writes): Adds text to the end of the file, creating it if needed.
- `fs.rm(p: path)` (can fail, writes): Deletes a file or folder, recursively; no error if it does not exist. Refuses "", /, ., .., ~ and the current folder.
- `fs.mkdir(p: path)` (can fail, writes): Creates the folder and its parents (like `mkdir -p`); no error if it already exists.
- `fs.copy(from: path, to: path)` (can fail, writes): Copies a file, or a folder recursively.
- `fs.move(from: path, to: path)` (can fail, writes): Moves or renames a file or folder.
- `fs.ls(dir: path) -> []str` (can fail): The names of the entries in the folder (without . and ..), sorted by bytes.
- `fs.walk(dir: path) -> []path` (can fail): Every file under the folder, recursively, as paths that start with `dir` as given, sorted.
- `fs.glob(pattern: str) -> []path`: The paths that match the pattern: `*` and `?` only in the last component; entries starting with `.` only if the pattern does; empty if nothing matches.
- `fs.temp_dir() -> path` (can fail): Creates a new temporary folder. Writes inside it run even with --dry-run.
- `fs.temp_file() -> path` (can fail): Creates a new temporary file. Writes to it run even with --dry-run.
- `fs.size(p: path) -> int` (can fail): The size in bytes; fails if the path does not exist.
- `fs.modified(p: path) -> int` (can fail): The last modification time, in Unix seconds; fails if the path does not exist.
- `fs.chmod(p: path, mode: str)` (can fail, writes): Unix: `chmod` ("755", "+x", "u+x"). Windows: checks the path and does nothing (there are no permission bits).
- `fs.replace(p: path, from: str, to: str)` (can fail, writes): Replaces every occurrence of literal text inside the file.

## Module hash

SHA-256 of text and files.

- `hash.sha256(text: str) -> str`: The SHA-256 of the text's UTF-8 bytes, in lowercase hex.
- `hash.sha256_file(p: path) -> str` (can fail): The SHA-256 of the file, in lowercase hex; fails if it does not exist.

## Module http

HTTP requests, with headers and a `bearer` token that never shows up in a command's arguments.

- `http.get(url: str, timeout: duration = 30s, headers: []str = [], bearer: secret = "") -> str` (can fail): Sends a GET and returns the body; fails on network errors and on status >= 400.
- `http.status(url: str, timeout: duration = 30s, headers: []str = [], bearer: secret = "") -> int` (can fail): Sends a GET and returns only the HTTP status code.
- `http.download(url: str, to: path, headers: []str = [], bearer: secret = "")` (can fail, writes): Downloads the URL into a file; fails on status >= 400 without leaving a partial file.
- `http.post(url: str, body: str, content_type: str = "application/json", timeout: duration = 30s, headers: []str = [], bearer: secret = "") -> str` (can fail, writes): Sends a POST and returns the response body; fails on status >= 400. With --dry-run it is only shown (and returns "").

## Module json

Reads JSON with paths like "a.b[0]", parsed by the script itself (no jq).

- `json.get(text: str, path: str) -> str` (can fail): The value at the path: text without quotes; numbers, bools, lists and objects as their JSON text. Fails if it is missing, null, or the text is not valid JSON.
- `json.get_list(text: str, path: str) -> []str` (can fail): The items of the list at the path, each as in `get` (null becomes "null").
- `json.keys(text: str, path: str) -> []str` (can fail): The keys of the object at the path, in the order of the text.
- `json.has(text: str, path: str) -> bool`: Whether the path exists and is not null (invalid JSON: false).
- `json.quote(text: str) -> str`: The text as a JSON string (quotes and escapes), for building JSON.

## Module log

Leveled messages on stderr.

- `log.info(items: any...)`: Prints `info: …` to stderr.
- `log.warn(items: any...)`: Prints `warning: …` to stderr.
- `log.error(items: any...)`: Prints `error: …` to stderr. It does not stop the script; `fail` does.
- `log.debug(items: any...)`: Prints `debug: …` to stderr, only with --verbose.

## Module math

Integer helpers.

- `math.min(a: int, b: int) -> int`: The smaller of two integers.
- `math.max(a: int, b: int) -> int`: The larger of two integers.
- `math.abs(n: int) -> int`: The absolute value.

## Module path

Path helpers. Properties like `.name` and `.parent` are read from `path` values.

- `path.abs(p: path) -> path`: The absolute path, with . and .. resolved.

## Module pkg

System package managers. Planned; the compiler refuses it for now (E090).

- `pkg.manager() -> str` (planned): The system's package manager: apt-get, dnf, yum, pacman, zypper, apk; brew; winget, choco, scoop; or "". Planned; the compiler refuses it for now (E090).
- `pkg.install(names: []str)` (can fail, writes, planned): Installs packages with the system's manager, with sudo on Linux when not root. Planned; the compiler refuses it for now (E090).

## Module proc

Programs on PATH.

- `proc.exists(cmd: str) -> bool`: Whether the program is on PATH.
- `proc.which(cmd: str) -> path` (can fail): The full path of the program; fails (exit code 127) if it is not on PATH.

## Module regex

Regular expressions in one portable syntax, checked by the compiler and identical on every target.

- `regex.test(text: str, pattern: str) -> bool`: Whether the pattern matches somewhere in the text. The pattern is fixed text in Nalu's regex syntax, checked by the compiler; write it in single quotes: `regex.test(v, '^\d+$')`.
- `regex.find(text: str, pattern: str) -> str` (can fail): The first match; fails if there is none. The pattern must have a single way to match (the compiler checks it).
- `regex.find_all(text: str, pattern: str) -> []str`: Every match, left to right; none gives an empty list. The pattern must have a single way to match and can't match empty text.
- `regex.groups(text: str, pattern: str) -> []str` (can fail): The groups `( … )` of the first match, in order (a group that took no part is ""); fails if there is no match.
- `regex.replace(text: str, pattern: str, new: str) -> str`: Replaces every match with `new`, taken literally (no `$1`). The pattern must have a single way to match and can't match empty text.

## Module semver

Version numbers such as 1.4.0 and v2.0.0-rc.1.

- `semver.compare(a: str, b: str) -> int` (can fail): Compares two versions: -1 if `a` is older, 0 if they are the same, 1 if `a` is newer. Numbers separated by dots, compared as numbers (`1.10` is newer than `1.9`; `1.2` equals `1.2.0`); a leading `v` and anything after `+` are ignored; a pre-release (`1.0.0-rc.1`) is older than its release. Fails if a text is not a version.

## Module sys

Architecture, user, admin and CI checks, the current folder.

- `sys.arch() -> str`: The CPU architecture: x64, arm64…
- `sys.hostname() -> str`: The machine's name.
- `sys.user() -> str`: The current user's name.
- `sys.is_admin() -> bool`: Whether the script runs as root / Administrator.
- `sys.require_admin()` (can fail): Fails with exit code 77 unless the script runs as root / Administrator.
- `sys.cpus() -> int`: The number of logical CPUs.
- `sys.is_ci() -> bool`: Whether the CI environment variable is set.
- `sys.cd(dir: path)` (can fail): Changes the script's current folder, until the end of the function or script.

## Module time

Timestamps, durations, formatting and waiting.

- `time.now() -> int`: The current time, in Unix seconds.
- `time.now_ms() -> int`: The current time, in Unix milliseconds.
- `time.since(t: int) -> duration`: The time elapsed since an instant from `time.now()` (second precision).
- `time.since_ms(t: int) -> duration`: The time elapsed since an instant from `time.now_ms()`.
- `time.format(fmt: str = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S", t: int = -1) -> str`: Formats an instant (`t = -1` is now). Only %Y %y %m %d %H %M %S %j %s %%.
- `time.sleep(d: duration)`: Waits for the given duration.
- `time.hour(t: int = -1) -> int`: The local hour, 0 to 23 (`t = -1` is now).

## Module ui

Questions for the user that fall back to a default without a terminal.

- `ui.confirm(question: str) -> bool`: Asks a yes/no question (`[y/N]`); false when there is no terminal.
- `ui.ask(question: str, fallback: str = "") -> str`: Asks for a line of text; returns `fallback` when there is no terminal.
- `ui.password(question: str) -> secret` (can fail): Asks for a secret, without echoing what is typed.
- `ui.choose(question: str, options: []str) -> str` (can fail): Shows a numbered menu and returns the chosen option.

## Type str

Text.

- `str.len() -> int`: The number of characters.
- `str.trim() -> str`: Removes whitespace from both ends.
- `str.trim_start() -> str`: Removes whitespace from the start.
- `str.trim_end() -> str`: Removes whitespace from the end.
- `str.upper() -> str`: An uppercase copy.
- `str.lower() -> str`: A lowercase copy.
- `str.contains(s: str) -> bool`: Whether `s` occurs in the text.
- `str.starts_with(s: str) -> bool`: Whether the text starts with `s`.
- `str.ends_with(s: str) -> bool`: Whether the text ends with `s`.
- `str.strip_prefix(s: str) -> str`: Removes `s` from the start, if it is there.
- `str.strip_suffix(s: str) -> str`: Removes `s` from the end, if it is there.
- `str.index_of(s: str) -> int`: The character index of the first `s`, or -1.
- `str.slice(start: int, end: int = end) -> str`: The characters from `start` up to, not including, `end`. Negative counts from the end; out of range is clamped.
- `str.split(sep: str) -> []str`: Splits on `sep`, keeping empty fields.
- `str.lines() -> []str`: Splits into lines (\n or \r\n), without the trailing empty line.
- `str.replace(from: str, to: str) -> str`: Replaces every occurrence of literal text.
- `str.replace_first(from: str, to: str) -> str`: Replaces the first occurrence of literal text.
- `str.repeat(n: int) -> str`: The text repeated `n` times.
- `str.pad_left(n: int, fill: str = " ") -> str`: Pads on the left with `fill` up to `n` characters.
- `str.pad_right(n: int, fill: str = " ") -> str`: Pads on the right with `fill` up to `n` characters.
- `str.to_int() -> int` (can fail): Parses a 64-bit integer, ignoring surrounding spaces; fails otherwise.
- `str.chars() -> []str`: One item per character.

## Type path

A file or folder path. `/` joins with the system's separator (`dirs.home() / ".config"`). Its properties (`.name`, `.stem`, `.ext`, `.parent`) only look at the text and never fail; anything on disk is in `fs` (`fs.exists(p)`, `fs.size(p)`).

- `path.name: str`: The last component, with its extension.
- `path.stem: str`: The last component, without its extension.
- `path.ext: str`: The extension without the dot; "" if there is none (dotfiles have none).
- `path.parent: path`: The containing folder; the root's parent is the root.
- `path.len() -> int`: The number of characters.
- `path.trim() -> str`: Removes whitespace from both ends.
- `path.trim_start() -> str`: Removes whitespace from the start.
- `path.trim_end() -> str`: Removes whitespace from the end.
- `path.upper() -> str`: An uppercase copy.
- `path.lower() -> str`: A lowercase copy.
- `path.contains(s: str) -> bool`: Whether `s` occurs in the text.
- `path.starts_with(s: str) -> bool`: Whether the text starts with `s`.
- `path.ends_with(s: str) -> bool`: Whether the text ends with `s`.
- `path.strip_prefix(s: str) -> str`: Removes `s` from the start, if it is there.
- `path.strip_suffix(s: str) -> str`: Removes `s` from the end, if it is there.
- `path.index_of(s: str) -> int`: The character index of the first `s`, or -1.
- `path.slice(start: int, end: int = end) -> str`: The characters from `start` up to, not including, `end`. Negative counts from the end; out of range is clamped.
- `path.split(sep: str) -> []str`: Splits on `sep`, keeping empty fields.
- `path.lines() -> []str`: Splits into lines (\n or \r\n), without the trailing empty line.
- `path.replace(from: str, to: str) -> str`: Replaces every occurrence of literal text.
- `path.replace_first(from: str, to: str) -> str`: Replaces the first occurrence of literal text.
- `path.repeat(n: int) -> str`: The text repeated `n` times.
- `path.pad_left(n: int, fill: str = " ") -> str`: Pads on the left with `fill` up to `n` characters.
- `path.pad_right(n: int, fill: str = " ") -> str`: Pads on the right with `fill` up to `n` characters.
- `path.to_int() -> int` (can fail): Parses a 64-bit integer, ignoring surrounding spaces; fails otherwise.
- `path.chars() -> []str`: One item per character.

## Type list

A list: `[1, 2, 3]`, typed `[]T` (`[]str`, `[]int`, `[][]str`). Indexing `xs[i]` fails when out of range.

- `[]T.len() -> int`: The number of items.
- `[]T.push(x: T)`: Adds the item to the end (only on a `var`).
- `[]T.pop() -> T` (can fail): Removes and returns the last item (only on a `var`); fails if the list is empty.
- `[]T.filter(f: (T) -> bool) -> []T`: The items for which `f` returns true.
- `[]T.map(f: (T) -> U) -> []U`: A new list with `f` applied to each item (`f` returns a scalar).
- `[]T.any(f: (T) -> bool) -> bool`: Whether `f` returns true for some item.
- `[]T.all(f: (T) -> bool) -> bool`: Whether `f` returns true for every item.
- `[]T.find(f: (T) -> bool) -> T` (can fail): The first item for which `f` returns true; fails if there is none.
- `[]T.contains(x: T) -> bool`: Whether the list has the item.
- `[]T.index_of(x: T) -> int`: The index of the first equal item, or -1.
- `[]T.join(sep: str) -> str`: Joins the items with `sep` (lists of scalars only).
- `[]T.sum() -> T`: The sum of a `[]int` or `[]duration`.
- `[]T.sort() -> []T`: Sorted ascending: text in ordinal order, numbers by value.
- `[]T.sort_by(f: (T) -> U) -> []T`: A stable sort by the key `f` returns (`int` or `str`).
- `[]T.reverse() -> []T`: The items in reverse order.
- `[]T.slice(start: int, end: int = end) -> []T`: The items from `start` up to, not including, `end`. Negative counts from the end; out of range is clamped.
- `[]T.unique() -> []T`: Without duplicates, keeping the first occurrence.
- `[]T.concat(other: []T) -> []T`: A new list with the items of this one followed by the items of `other`.
- `[]T.first() -> T` (can fail): The first item; fails if the list is empty.
- `[]T.last() -> T` (can fail): The last item; fails if the list is empty.

## Type map

A map: `{ "a": 1 }`, typed `map[K]V`; keys are `str`, `int` or an enum, values are scalars or lists of scalars (`map[str][]str`). `m[k]` fails when the key does not exist; `m[k] = v` writes.

- `map[K]V.len() -> int`: The number of items.
- `map[K]V.has(k: K) -> bool`: Whether the key exists.
- `map[K]V.remove(k: K)`: Removes the key (only on a `var`); no error if it does not exist.
- `map[K]V.keys() -> []K`: The keys, in insertion order.
- `map[K]V.values() -> []V`: The values, in insertion order.

## Type int

A 64-bit integer.

- Arithmetic: `+ - * / %` (`/` truncates toward zero); comparison: `== != < <= > >=`.
- From text: `s.to_int()` (can fail); to text: `"{n}"`.

## Type bool

`true` or `false`.

- `&&`, `||` and `!`; `if` takes only `bool` (compare explicitly: `n != 0`, `s != ""`).

## Type duration

A length of time: `500ms`, `30s`, `1m30s`, `2h`, `7d`.

- `+`, `-` and comparison between durations; `d / 1s` gives an `int`; `d * 2` scales it.
- Interpolation shows the shortest form: `"{d}"` → `1m30s`.

## Type secret

Text that is never printed, logged or passed in a command's arguments; it reaches commands only through stdin (`token | $ cmd`).

- Made with `secret(text)`, `ui.password(q)` or a `param` of type `secret` (also read from `NALU_<NAME>`).
- It cannot be interpolated, printed or compared; pass it to a command with `token | $ cmd` or to a function that takes `secret`.

## Type enum

Declared with `enum Name { a, b }`. Cases are written `Name.a` (just `a` inside `match`), interpolation gives the case's name (`"{x}"`), and every enum has `Name.parse(text)`.

- `Enum.parse(text: str) -> Enum` (can fail): `Type.parse("prod")`: the case with that name; fails if there is none.

## Type error

The failure being handled, as `err` inside `catch { … }` and in `catch fail "…{err}"`.

- `err.message: str`: the failure's message (what `{err}` shows).
- `err.code: int`: the exit code; 1 by default, the command's own code for commands.

## Built-ins

- `print(items: any...)`: Writes the items to standard output, separated by spaces, with a newline at the end.
- `fmt(template: str, items: any...) -> str`: Replaces each `{}` in the template with the next item (only `{}`, no format specifiers).
- `secret(text: str) -> secret`: Turns text into a secret: never printed, never passed in a command's arguments.

## Keywords and constants

| | |
|---|---|
| `let name = value` | Declares a name that cannot change. Use `var` for one that can. |
| `var name = value` | Declares a variable that can change (`=`, `+=`, `.push(…)`). |
| `fn name(param: type) -> type { … }` | Declares a function. It can fail if something inside it can fail without `catch`; the compiler works that out. |
| `return value` | Ends the function, returning the value. |
| `struct Name { field: type }` | Declares a record type with fields and methods (`fn` inside it, with `self`). |
| `enum Name { a, b, c }` | Declares a type with a fixed set of cases: `Name.a`, `Name.parse("a")`. |
| `param name: type = default` | A command-line option of the script: `--name value`. The `///` comment above it becomes its `--help` text; without a default it is required. |
| `if cond { … } else { … }` | Runs a block when the condition is true. As a value, both branches give the value and `else` is required. |
| `else { … }` | The branch of an `if` that runs when the condition is false. |
| `for x in list { … }` | Repeats the block for each item of a list, each `key, value` of a map, or each number of a range (`0..10`). |
| `for x in list` | Separates the loop names from what is being iterated. |
| `while cond { … }` | Repeats the block while the condition is true. |
| `match value { pattern => result }` | Runs the first arm that matches the value: text, numbers, ranges, durations, bools, enum cases or `Struct { field: pattern }`. `_` matches anything, a name (`n => …`) takes the value, and `pattern if condition =>` adds a guard. |
| `break` | Leaves the innermost loop. |
| `continue` | Skips to the next iteration of the innermost loop. |
| `fail "message"` | Fails with a message (and optionally `code: n`). The function fails, or the script stops, unless a caller handles it with `catch`. |
| `risky() catch fallback` | Handles a failure on its left: `catch value`, `catch fail "…"`, `catch ignore` or `catch { … }` (with `err`). Without `catch`, failures propagate: the function fails, or the script stops. |
| `catch ignore` | Handles a failure by doing nothing. |
| `try { … } catch …` | Groups several lines under one `catch`: the first failure jumps to the handler. |
| `defer call()` | Runs the call when the function or script ends, even after a failure or Ctrl+C. |
| `parallel for x in list { … }` | Runs the tasks at the same time and waits for all of them; if any fail, it fails with every error. `parallel(max: n)` limits how many run at once. |
| `retry(3, every: 5s) { … }` | Runs the block again until it does not fail, up to n times; then fails with the last error. |
| `native { bash: "…", powershell: "…" }` | Raw shell code for each target, when the standard library has no portable way. |
| `test "name" { … }` | A test, run by `nalu test`. Use `assert cond` and `assert_fails(call)` inside it. |
| `use "lib.nalu"` | Brings in the `fn`, `struct`, `enum` and `test` declarations of another file. `use` lines go at the start of the file and the path is relative to it; the script still compiles to one self-contained file per target. |
| `self` | The value a method was called on (inside `fn` declared in a `struct`). Read-only. |
| `true` | The `bool` value true. |
| `false` | The `bool` value false. |
| `os: str` | The target system: "linux", "macos" or "windows". A compile-time constant, so `if os == …` keeps only the matching branch in each script. |
| `dry_run: bool` | Whether the script runs with --dry-run (commands and writes are only shown). |
| `args: []str` | The command-line arguments that are not options (and everything after `--`). |
| `err: error` | The failure being handled, inside `catch { … }` and `catch fail "…{err}"`: `err.message` and `err.code`. |
| `exit(code)` | Ends the script now with the exit code (runs `defer` first). |
| `embed("file.txt") -> str` | The contents of a text file, read at compile time (the path is relative to the .nalu file). |
| `assert cond` | In a test: fails the test when the condition is false, showing the condition. |
| `assert_fails(call)` | In a test: fails the test when the call does not fail. |
| `_ => …` | In a `match`, matches any value the arms above did not. |
